P1.evidence: A setter pre-qualified this prospect, so P1a applies and it inverted: rather than reading the notes back, the rep asked the prospect to supply them — 'I'm sure Kim has probably mentioned a few details to you.' The prospect later confirmed he had given Kim information the rep did not have: 'I forgot the details to Kim.' The frame ran in the usual compressed three-part form and no agreement was sought. Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: By some distance the best baseline in this batch and the one to use as the coaching reference. Age, height and weight asked in sequence. Work asked properly and including the posture check the other calls all skip: 'what do you do for work?' followed by 'are you sitting down primarily for those, say, six, seven hours?'. The training week asked specifically — 'Monday to Sunday, what does the training regimen look like specifically?' — producing a full day-by-day picture. Diet asked with a useful optimisation framing. Sleep asked. Energy asked. And P2d was run to completion for once, including duration and location: 'where in your body do you experience pains?', 'is that in the same regions?', 'How long has that been going on for?'. The single miss is P2c: health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked, so the chiropractic care surfaced only as an aside.

P3.evidence: Persistent and well run against a difficult prospect. The bridge ran cleanly — 'would you say that you're 100% living up to your athletic potential?' — and when the prospect answered the vision question with logistics, the rep refused it and reframed twice: 'I understand what you need, right? And we can touch on that in a moment. But in terms of who you want to show up as, paint that picture.' That produced the genuinely useful ten-out-of-ten picture: less pain on standing, ten rounds of sparring without fading, explosiveness between rounds. Ripple ran to the children and the wife. P3g is only partial because the rep pushed for a deeper why three separate ways — 'why do you even want to be more athletic', 'why is that important for you', 'why do you want to get there faster' — and the prospect genuinely had none: 'I don't know. I guess I'm wired that way.' That is not a rep failure; it is a prospect with no pain to leverage, and the process has no route for that case. No reflect-back was attempted.

P4.evidence: Like the Roy Norman call, this phase is a poor fit and was not forced. There is no adherence failure to diagnose — the prospect trains seven times a week, sleeps eight hours, and his current diet has produced six to eight pounds of loss — so P4c is marked not applicable rather than missed. P4e landed: he named the gap himself and precisely, 'what I need is what program do I need to follow, right? And it's not static.' P4f ran well and was tailored to him: 'what is the rationale in terms of wanting to get outside help as opposed to using, you're an engineer, right? ChatGPT, Claude, YouTube, information is so abundant.' The answer — 'if it doesn't work out, that's what I'll probably end up doing' — was an explicit statement that the free route is the fallback, and it was not built on.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame; the sixth consecutive call in this batch without one. The want-or-need question ran and returned the single most diagnostic answer of the batch: 'That's a want, not a need. Like you said, seven is pretty good, right? So from a need perspective, I don't need it, but that's a want.' The script's response to that is phase 5 — make the cost of inaction real, since a prospect who does not need it will not pay. Instead the rep said 'Right. All right, man. Do you have a pen or paper?' and went straight into the pillars. The material was there too: the prospect had already supplied his own consequence frame, 'at 45, I'm fine. I'm still good. What's going to happen at 55?'. Nobody picked it up.

P6.evidence: The alignment check ran before the price, correctly, and returned a reasonable seven to eight with a stated caveat about not having seen the programme. But the scripted belief question was never asked in its own form, the all-in question was never asked at all, and P6c is only partial because the prospect had explicitly said twenty minutes earlier that he did not need this. Under the script that is hesitation requiring a return to phase 5, and phase 5 had not been run.

P11.evidence: No sale of any product, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: A clear money trigger and none of the play ran. No isolation, no how-not-whether reframe, no payment-plan invitation and no element of the financial picture. The rep instead disqualified and downsold. On the playbook this scores a miss, and the honest assessment is that the miss was correct: a $150 per month budget against a $4,000 minimum is roughly a twenty-seven-fold gap, and no financing structure closes it. This is the same rep who, the previous day, ran the complete financial interrogation on a prospect in Chapter 7 bankruptcy proceedings and closed him. The judgement applied here was sound; the inconsistency between the two is the finding.
No request for thinking time; he declined on budget immediately and finally.
Wife mentioned in relation to his boxing, never as an approval gate for the purchase.
Timing was not the blocker — 'just get started. Getting started is 50% of the battle.'
No fear or doubt about capability; if anything the reverse, since he was confident he could execute any programme given to him.

Logged as a positive and as a gap. There is no scripted disqualification path in the playbook — every objection play is built to convert — and here the rep improvised one and got it right: 'If you were to really, like, put gun to my head, I don't really think you need the one-on-one coaching like that. Again, it's not Kim's fault, it's not anyone's fault, it's just, it is what it is, right? Some people aren't the best fit for this, but I still want to make sure you're supported in some kind of capacity.' That is the behaviour the script should require and does not, and its absence is what produced the Brandon Johnson outcome twenty-four hours earlier. Recommend adding an explicit disqualification branch with a stated budget threshold.

Reduced-scope objection, now the third occurrence in this batch after Roy Norman and Soneel Raj. The prospect wanted pillar one only and said so plainly, having his nutrition already customised from India and considering himself headstrong enough not to need accountability or community. There is no training-only tier. The rep improvised the nearest thing — Primal University at $200 per month — which is directionally the right answer, but he could not demonstrate it ('I can't show anything') and the prospect left saying 'I'm still kind of figuring out what exactly it provides or not.' Three prospects in two days have now asked to buy part of the bundle.

notes: The strongest baseline and one of the strongest phase 3 performances in the batch, against a prospect who was never going to buy at these prices. Two things worth separating. The rep's commercial judgement was good — he disqualified rather than discounting, which is the opposite of what he did with Brandon Johnson the day before, and the difference in treatment between a business owner with a $150 budget and a man in bankruptcy proceedings should be examined. The process failure is narrow and repeated: the prospect said 'that's a want, not a need' and 'I don't need it', which is the trigger for phase 5, and the rep went straight to the pillars. Six calls, six missing consequence frames. That is a training gap, not six individual lapses.
